## 本日債市主線

聯準會週三啟動2023年7月以來首次升息，並示意可能繼續緊縮，帶動短天期美國公債價格下跌、殖利率曲線趨平。2年期殖利率收高7個基點至4.74%，10年期微升1個基點至5.01%，30年期則小降1個基點至5.35%。Kevin Warsh對通膨的強硬表態推高市場預期的近期資金成本，卻未引發長天期公債再度全面遭到拋售。

決策前公布的美國零售支出明顯反彈，進口物價也轉強，但房市與區域服務業已呈現明確弱勢。油價下跌略為改善通膨前景；實質殖利率上升的同時，長期通膨補償反而下降。信用市場同樣守穩，美國投資等級債與硬通貨新興市場債利差明顯收窄，高收益債利差也小幅收窄。聯準會利率路徑轉趨緊縮，投資人卻仍願意提供融資，另一筆鉅額AI基礎設施貸款便是例證。

## 聯準會升息，美債曲線趨平

聯邦公開市場委員會一致決議升息25個基點，將目標區間調至3.75%至4%。這次升息本在市場普遍預期之中，對後續定價影響更大的，是Warsh將其定義為撤除寬鬆。若升息前的利率仍在支持經濟成長，首次升息就未必足以抑制通膨。

Warsh指出，太多商品與服務在過去6個月及12個月的年化漲幅仍超過3%，夏季數據尚不足以讓他相信基礎通膨趨勢已有實質改善。他也認為經濟似乎正在轉強。委員會強調，國內支出具韌性，資本投資強勁，生產力成長穩健；就業增加速度跟得上勞動力擴張，失業率變動不大。

官員預測顯示，繼續升息獲得廣泛支持。在提交近期利率預測的18位官員中，16位預期2026年底前至少再升息一次，其中4位預期再升息兩次。年底利率預測中位數由6月的3.8%升至4.1%，2027年也維持4.1%；8位官員則將明年利率定在4.4%。Warsh再次未提交利率預測點，因此這組分布不包含他本人偏好的終點。

委員會也將年底核心通膨預測中位數由3.3%調高至3.4%，2026年GDP成長預測則由2.2%小幅調升至2.3%。即使開始緊縮，通膨回到2%的預期時間仍延後一年至2029年。這組預測反映官員認為通膨更為持久，而非因預期經濟即將急遽萎縮而採取行動。

決議公布前，美債原本上漲，2年期殖利率一度在4.60%附近，之後升至4.74%，完全逆轉稍早走勢。10年期也在Warsh記者會期間回吐先前的殖利率降幅。到紐約下午5時收盤，5年期殖利率上升3個基點至4.86%，漲幅介於短端的大幅上升與10年期的小幅變動之間。

2年與10年期利差收窄6個基點至27個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄8個基點至61個基點，後者創2025年3月以來最窄收盤水準。過去一個月，2年期殖利率累計上升57個基點，30年期卻僅升10個基點；隨著預期政策利率路徑上移，曲線已明顯趨平。

抗通膨公債的變化說明，10年期名目殖利率變動有限，不代表借款成本普遍減輕。10年期實質殖利率上升6個基點至2.68%，損益兩平通膨率則下降5個基點至2.33%。投資人要求更高的通膨調整後報酬，同時願意接受較低的長期通膨補償。油價下降與央行態度更積極，都有利於壓低後者；但實質殖利率走高，仍提高了投資與其他長期支出所需達到的報酬門檻。

決議後，利率交換市場反映明年年中前還會升息三次，較決議前多一次，貨幣市場則賦予10月升息約50%的機率。這條路徑比聯準會預測更積極。凱投宏觀的Stephen Brown預期下次升息在12月，2027年再升息一次，理由是官員低估了失業率進一步下降的可能性。

摩根資產管理的Priya Misra認為，市場焦點已從懷疑聯準會公信力，轉向擔心抗通膨行動的經濟影響。RBC Global Asset Management的Andrzej Skiba則認為，初步重新定價過後，清楚的政策溝通最終可能支撐長天期美債。Evercore的Krishna Guha形容整場記者會一貫鷹派，但也提醒，將升息稱為撤除寬鬆，反而讓最終利率水準更不明確。

對於先前長天期殖利率上升，Warsh並不認為可以單純歸因於市場對央行失去信心。他列舉經濟活動轉強、資本支出激增與資金競爭，並明確提及超大型雲端業者，也指出地緣政治熱點與成品油價格的影響。他否認委員會是被市場定價迫使採取行動。

美元隨短端利率重新定價而走強，美元指數上漲0.62%至100.267，標普500指數下跌0.45%。半導體股上漲0.63%，幫助那斯達克100指數小漲0.03%作收；黃金期貨則下跌0.16%至每盎司$4,325.80。政策前景轉緊之下，各資產報酬仍有差異，並非風險資產全面遭到拋售。

摩根資產管理的Bob Michele則逆近期賣壓而行。他週三表示，團隊已開始買進美國、日本與澳洲的長天期債券。這項判斷仰賴貨幣緊縮重建信心，以及中東局勢可能在美國期中選舉接近時趨於穩定；他也將美國財政部買回公債視為穩定市場的力量。

美國總統川普在升息後要求將利率降至1%或以下，起初未直接點名批評Warsh。週三稍晚他表示已與主席談過，仍對其有信心，但指控理事會抱持政治敵意。聯準會一致通過決議之際，總統也再度要求採取截然不同的利率政策。

## 消費支出反彈，房市持續轉弱

8月零售銷售在聯準會開會前提供了需求較強的證據：月增1.2%，創3月以來最大增幅，高於路透共識預估的0.8%；7月降幅則由0.6%修正為0.5%。更值得注意的是支出組成，排除汽車、汽油、建材與餐飲服務的核心零售銷售大增1.4%，遠高於預估的0.4%，也是2024年9月以來最強增幅。

成長預測隨即上修。高盛將第三季GDP年化成長率預估提高0.5個百分點至3.0%，摩根大通則由2.75%調升至3.5%。汽油與汽車以外的支出強勁，意味數據不只是家庭多花錢買燃料，也使「高能源成本與低迷信心已導致支出全面退縮」的假設更難成立。

進口物價則強化升息背後的通膨理由。8月進口物價月增0.7%，高於共識預估的0.4%，7月修正後為月減0.3%；年增率由修正後的6.1%升至7.0%，創2022年8月以來最快。出口物價月增0.6%，同樣高於預估的0.5%，前月修正後為月減1.4%；年增率由前期修正後的8.1%升至8.6%。在消費反彈之外，貿易商品價格也擴大了當日成本壓力的證據。

不過，其他數據顯示經濟強勢並不全面。紐約聯準銀行9月服務業活動指數由0.5降至-8.7，反映區域經濟的一部分正在惡化。7月企業庫存增加0.8%，高於預估的0.3%及前期修正後的0.1%；排除汽車的零售庫存也增加0.8%，高於預估的0.7%，前期則減少0.5%。加快補庫存能推升統計上的產出，但與零售銷售所呈現的最終需求強勁並不相同。

房市已在承受融資成本上升。美國抵押貸款銀行協會資料顯示，截至9月11日當週，30年期房貸合約利率上升12個基點至6.97%，為2025年5月以來最高。房貸申請總量繼前週下降2.7%後，再降4.1%；購屋貸款申請減少0.8%，轉貸申請大減8.8%，降至2025年5月以來最低。

9月NAHB／富國銀行房市指數也下跌3點至32，低於共識預估的34，追平2022年底以來低點。未來銷售預期降至2023年初以來最弱，目前銷售轉差，買方看屋人潮維持低迷。最大住宅興建區域南部，以及中西部、東北部，建商信心均下降，西部則小幅改善。

建商增加讓利，卻仍擺脫不了成本壓力。提供促銷優惠的比例由63%升至66%，降價比例由35%升至38%。NAHB主席Bill Owens指出，建材與燃料成本上升，勞工短缺也持續存在；部分市場加強移民執法，甚至使合法勞工不敢到工地上班。需求疲弱的同時，這些供給限制仍推高建築成本。

面向消費者的企業表現同樣分歧。零售支出雖然強勁，標普500非必需消費品指數仍有超過四分之一成分股處於52週低點。CIBC Capital Markets估計，AI投資今年將對全年通膨貢獻約0.4個百分點。這項估計指出家庭需求以外的物價壓力來源，也有助解釋，為何整體支出具韌性，受融資成本與消費者財力限制影響的企業卻仍陷困境。

週三油價走勢則有利於減輕壓力。以債市收盤時點計，布蘭特原油下跌3.47%至每桶$104.98，西德州原油下跌4.09%至$101.50。回落減弱了眼前的能源價格衝擊，但布蘭特近一個月仍上漲18.59%。沙烏地阿美已售出約2,000萬桶原油給亞洲煉油商，安排在荷姆茲海峽以外提貨，這是東西向輸油管線停運後的交付調整。

美國石油庫存也稍微緩解了供應吃緊的情勢。EIA資料顯示，截至9月11日當週，原油庫存減少64萬桶，少於預估的160萬桶降幅；汽油庫存增加79.4萬桶，市場原估減少100萬桶，餾分油庫存增加158.5萬桶，也高於預估增加10萬桶。成品油庫存累積，對海外供應中斷與高燃料價格形成一定緩衝。

週三稍晚的報導進一步交代沙烏地修復計畫的時程。阿美正設法繞過全長1,200公里東西向管線的受損段，目標在數日內恢復約一半輸送能力，約六週內全面恢復運作。近期關注重點已從無限期停運，轉為能否按計畫局部重啟。

## AI融資擴大，長天期公司債供給縮減

據知情人士透露，10家銀行正為Blackstone與Alphabet支持的雲端事業Crux AI提供$220億貸款，用來購買Google的張量處理器，債務由晶片價值及客戶合約支撐。這筆大額新資金投入的是資料中心內的處理器，而非僅限於建築工程。

參貸銀行包括高盛、三井住友銀行、巴克萊、法國巴黎銀行與加拿大豐業銀行，並透過聯貸引入其他貸款機構分攤曝險。其中部分銀行另提供$10億循環信用額度；主要貸款日後可能透過投資等級債市場，轉為期限更長的機構融資。

Crux獲Blackstone初始股權資金$50億支持，目標2027年讓500MW容量上線，規劃中的客戶包括AI實驗室，將與CoreWeave、Nebius等雲端運算容量供應商競爭。但主要預定資料中心場址仍有延誤；這些融資所支持的晶片與客戶承諾，能否實際部署，仍取決於設施何時可用。

同類交易的潛在規模也持續增加。在Broadcom支持、用於Anthropic租用TPU的$350億融資案之後，市場正討論另一筆超過$600億的晶片融資架構。OpenAI則另外就新一輪募資展開初步洽談，估值擬超過$1.2兆；若完成股權募資，將增加其收購空間，也能延後上市。

歐洲正準備承接更大的債務融資角色。高盛估計，年底前歐洲市場可能迎來$50億至$100億資料中心債券，2027年發行量將更大。摩根大通與高盛都已組成專責團隊爭取業務。根據Dealogic與高盛研究，歐洲AI相關債務約占高收益債發行量5%，美國則為19%。

專案規模愈來愈大，過往開發案使用的融資組合已難以支應，葡萄牙規劃中的1.2GWStart Campus就是一例。高盛的Miriam Wheeler表示，歐洲一座新建100至200MW資料中心，可能至少需要$10億至$20億的債務交易；更大的專案則須同時運用投資等級、高收益與144A市場。她估計，歐洲占全球AI建置的比重可能由10%升至最高25%。彭博行業研究則估計，截至2035年，歐洲雲端基礎設施、資料中心及其他關鍵科技的潛在需求約為$3兆。

信用投資人仍在區分個別專案。CoreWeave債券是歐洲高收益市場唯一的資料中心債券，自主要客戶Meta傳出發展競爭性雲端基礎設施業務後，一直在面額以下交易。RBC BlueBay的Sid Chhabra強調，盡職調查須採高標準，有環境投資要求的貸款機構則嚴格檢視電力與用水。隨著潛在發行量擴大，客戶集中度與工程完工風險也成為授信考量。

另一筆規模較小、已完成的融資，顯示結構合適仍可吸引需求。部分歐洲投資人先參訪Equinix位於斯勞的設施，其7月發行的£2.8億資產擔保證券便吸引超過£5.1億訂單。這些買家在更大規模供給可能到來前，先檢視實體資產與營運，並未將所有AI相關借款人視為同一類。

週三稍晚，EQT董事長表示，公司計畫2030年前在印度投資$500億，其中約$300億投入資料中心，另有$50億投入再生能源，並將大舉投資Gautam Adani的資料中心事業。這些規劃結合運算容量與電力，顯示資本需求不只在晶片。

相較之下，傳統長天期公司債發行正在縮減，發行人不願長期鎖定高借款成本。9月美國高評級債發行中，長天期債券僅占5%，為至少2020年以來最低，發行金額也不到去年同期的一半；3至10年到期券種占比則由51%升至60%。據市場知情人士透露，企業與銀行陸續放棄原定的長天期發行計畫。

供給稀少，使這類債券一旦發行便獲需求支撐。最新披露的Aon週一融資細節顯示，$20億、2056年到期券吸引逾$140億訂單，之後在次級市場的表現也優於其他期限。GSK上週發行$5億30年期債券，訂單達發行額的15倍。企業財務主管減少供給之際，壽險與退休基金仍需要長天期資產。

企業融資與政府借款之間的相互影響也愈來愈重要。彭博最新計算顯示，Alphabet、Amazon、Meta、Microsoft與Oracle在五年間合計增加約$4,120億債務義務。因此，Warsh提到的資本競爭，不只是投機性專案，也涉及高評級借款人大幅擴張。

富國銀行的新研究則檢視成長能否緩解財政壓力。經濟學家Tom Porcelli與Michael Pugliese在週二報告中估算，未來十年若要穩定美國債務占GDP比率，每年經濟成長須達3%至3.5%，且稅收或支出政策不得有重大變動。他們指出，勞動力擴張放慢之下，要達到這樣的成長率，勞動生產力必須創下史上最快增長。當前投資雖支撐經濟，但這項估計顯示，靠成長抵銷債務負擔的成立條件相當嚴苛。

Xerox面臨的則是更迫切的資產負債表抉擇。Starteepo的Frantisek Bostl所管理基金持有約7.3%的經濟權益，正敦促公司聘請顧問，評估金融服務業務的合資、資本合作或出售方案。他認為所得資金可用於減債並簡化公司結構。Xerox表示將審議提案；Bostl則說，若第三季前未落實，將探索其他選項。目前仍由股東推動，尚未達成出售協議。

## 各國央行面對不同通膨訊號

英國8月CPI年增率升至3.1%，創五個月高點，符合路透共識預估，但基礎指標較為穩定：核心通膨連續第四個月維持2.6%，服務業通膨維持3.4%。生產者物價較令人擔心，產出價格年增3.7%，高於所有預測，7月則修正為3.3%；投入價格通膨達6.1%，7月也由4.9%上修至5.8%。

對英國央行而言，這種分歧意味能源與運輸漲價，尚未讓上述廣泛的基礎消費物價指標同步加速。週三市場定價顯示，9月17日升息25個基點的機率約20%，年底前升息兩次的機率則約75%。眼前是否升息，與稍後是否繼續緊縮，仍是兩個不同判斷。

英國債務結構的新分析也說明，減少長債供給為何未帶來持久紓解。隨發行轉向短天期、退休基金需求轉弱，政府債務加權平均到期年限已由2020年的逾18年降至約11年。彭博經濟研究估計，借款成本與通膨升高，可能耗去政府為符合財政規則所保留的£236億緩衝空間中的約£160億。

RBC策略師Megum Muhic認為，在更廣泛的全球壓力下，即使英國央行停止出售長天期公債，影響也僅屬邊際。不過，30年期英國公債相對同年期利率交換的利差，今年以來大致穩定，削弱了「殖利率上升全數反映英國特有財政風險溢價急遽惡化」的說法。債務到期年限縮短與財政緩衝減少，仍各自構成風險。

歐元區薪資數據則抵銷了部分能源通膨疑慮。第二季勞動成本年增率由第一季的3.3%降至3.1%。歐洲央行薪資追蹤指標預測，2027年第一、二季薪資增幅分別為2.7%與2.8%，只是溫和回升，並非重返2024年5.2%的高峰。央行說明，2026年上半年讀值偏低，部分是先前一次性給付消失所致，這項影響會在下半年完全消退。

因此，新數據有助區分比較基期帶來的薪資增幅回升，以及對能源衝擊的全面反應。歐洲央行認為，薪資成長約3%大致符合2%通膨。它仍警告，衝擊若拖長，可能改變工資與定價行為，但目前追蹤指標幾乎未顯示這種加速已經發生。

歐洲公債在聯準會決議前回升。歐洲接近中午時，德國10年期殖利率下降3個基點至3.504%；週二曾觸及3.5723%，為2009年6月以來最高。法國殖利率下降3個基點至4.468%，相對德國利差為96個基點；義大利殖利率下降4個基點至4.38%。油價下跌緩解公債壓力，但未消除法國偏高的風險溢價，市場也仍預期歐洲央行將進一步緊縮。

加拿大央行新公布的9月2日議事摘要，更明確界定了通膨觸發條件。官員當時將利率維持在2.25%，認為幾乎沒有證據顯示汽油漲價已廣泛轉嫁至其他商品與服務。但他們一致認為，能源成本持續偏高會增加外溢風險，若對消費物價產生更廣泛影響，可能需要貨幣政策回應。整體通膨一直在3%附近，核心通膨則接近2%目標。

理事會成員對經濟閒置程度意見不一，但即使成長範圍擴大、就業增加穩健，仍判斷經濟處於供給過剩。他們表示，美國新關稅涵蓋加拿大對美商品出口約5%，將傷害受影響企業與信心，但整體直接衝擊可能不大，財政措施也能抵銷部分損害。加拿大的反制關稅集中在中間投入品與有本土替代品的產品，預期通膨影響有限。

另一項獨立的貿易政策進展，是歐盟執委會主席范德賴恩邀請加拿大成為歐盟首個準會員。現行條約並未定義這個擬議身分，其對投資與貿易的意義將取決於實際條件，而非名稱。加拿大總理卡尼預定週四向歐洲議會發表演說。

日本8月貿易數據在央行決策前顯示，能源帳單愈來愈高。進口額年增28.0%，創2022年11月以來最快，高於預估的26.3%；出口額年增19.3%，高於共識預估的18.2%，並連續12個月年增。貿易逆差達¥1.106兆，高於預估的¥1.053兆。

其中，原油進口量僅增加3.6%，金額卻大增58.7%，顯示油款壓力主要來自價格。路透引述的分析師警告，進口時滯可能讓9月起的成本轉嫁加劇，為日本央行緊縮預期增添新的觀察依據。

南非通膨預期調查則朝有利方向變化。經濟研究局公布，兩年後平均通膨預期由3.9%降至3.8%，但仍高於央行3%目標。遠期利率協議反映的9月23日升息25個基點機率，由週二56%降至52%。Amundi的Nicolas Dahan警告，再次按兵不動可能損害公信力；總裁Lesetja Kganyago則主張，面對油價與天候衝擊交疊，應採審慎、適度的回應。

美國收盤後，巴西央行一致決議將Selic利率調降25個基點至13.75%，是連續第五次同幅降息，3月以來累計寬鬆125個基點。央行將政策相關期間、即2028年第一季通膨預測維持3.2%，本輪最終降息幅度，仍取決於確保通膨收斂至目標所需的資訊。

週三稍早公布的巴西7月經濟活動指數月減0.22%，連續第二個月下降，略遜於預期的月減0.2%，但仍比去年同期高1.14%。新一輪轉弱支持降息，10月選舉卻帶來匯率不確定性。高盛的Alberto Ramos表示，雷亞爾若急貶，可能導致暫停降息。XP的Caio Megale預期今年再降兩次、每次25個基點；Itaú的Diogo Guillen則傾向停在13.75%，但也認為匯率與通膨預測若穩定，仍可容許進一步寬鬆。

亞洲週四清晨，國際貨幣基金呼籲澳洲央行，必要時仍應準備升息。其第四條款磋商代表團將2026、2027年成長預測，分別由2%與1.7%下修至1.9%與1.6%，但仍認為通膨風險偏上行，也不確定金融情勢是否已具足夠限制性。代表團還指出，資料中心投資會增加營建壓力，並可能推高電費；財政節制則有助通膨下降。

香港隨後在週四早間跟進聯準會，將基本利率提高25個基點至4.25%，以維護聯繫匯率。不過，房貸定價還取決於商業銀行貸款利率與本地流動性。1個月期Hibor已升至2.95%，為近三個月最高，港元則在允許區間弱方附近交易。美國報酬提高持續帶動美元需求，而香港借款成本上升也威脅房市復甦。

## 主權融資與本地市場各尋買盤

羅馬尼亞官員向投資人表示，今年國際發債可能減少，帶動其外幣債上漲。據熟悉倫敦會議的人士透露，財政部國庫主管Stefan Nanu表示，政府組成、政治前景更明朗之前，不會再發行歐洲債券。消息傳出後，2051年與2053年到期券成為新興市場表現最強的債券之一。

羅馬尼亞原訂外部融資目標€100億，目前已透過國際歐元與美元券籌得約€50億，官方資料另外列出約€20億私募。國內借款增加，降低了近期追加國際發債的需要。供給消息雖支撐價格，卻未解決如何就可信的2027年預算達成共識。

相對估值顯示投資人承擔這些風險獲得多少補償。羅馬尼亞5年期CDS週二為144個基點，低於4月底的167個基點，卻遠高於阿曼與印尼約85個基點。主要信評機構仍給予羅馬尼亞最低一級的投資等級評等，但其外債交易水準已與若干投機等級主權相近。2年期本幣債殖利率6.52%，比波蘭高約180個基點，比捷克高235個基點。

Aberdeen的Viktor Szabo認為，若政策利率維持穩定、財政表現持續強勁，羅馬尼亞具有價值，但2027年預算若缺乏說服力，可能引發降評。法國興業銀行的Juan Orts則預期，下個月標普審查時不會降評。眼前漲勢來自預期供給減少，改善能否持久，仍取決於這些不同的財政判斷。

塞內加爾則取得納入本幣債基準指數的新管道。摩根大通即將推出的Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets Edge指數，將納入兩檔合計價值$6.54億的塞內加爾工具，給予該國0.34%權重。非洲將占指數近45%，其中埃及、摩洛哥各占8%。整體指數將追蹤約$3,280億、425檔工具，涵蓋26個市場及24種貨幣。

此次納入的是本地債務，塞內加爾打算將其排除於外債處理範圍之外。摩根大通另一項衡量中，該國主權債相對美債風險溢價仍達1,639個基點。因此，取得指數資格引進的是另一群潛在投資人，並未改變外部債權談判的狀態。

印度方面，新的預測進一步反映印度央行先前已宣布收回流動性的影響。ICICI Securities Primary Dealership與IDFC First Bank預期，10年期殖利率年底前可能升至7.25%，高於週二拋售後所述的7.08%。花旗將預期首次升息時間由12月提前至10月。QuantEco估計，仍需再吸收₹2兆流動性，可能透過短期外匯交換、穩定證券或現金管理國庫券進行。

法國巴黎銀行策略師Chandresh Jain預期，銀行減碼先前以多餘資金累積的部位，將使3至10年期債券持續承壓，其中3至5年期殖利率可能比10年期升得更快。新公布的外資持有資料顯示，符合指數資格的債券，週五流出₹473億後，週二持有額又減少₹247億，顯示本地利率調整之際，外資也在撤出。

中國人民銀行行長潘功勝對貸款疲弱提出結構性解釋，而非新的刺激承諾。他表示，房地產與地方政府融資需求萎縮的影響，大於新興產業借款增加。貸款餘額超過人民幣280兆元，但對上半年成長貢獻逾40%的高科技製造與綠色科技，較不依賴銀行信貸。

潘功勝強調融資組成已改變：2025年社會融資規模增量中，貸款占45%，債券與股票合計占47%，首次超過貸款。他形容融資條件相對寬鬆，總量擴張放慢則有助穩定槓桿。這項論點意味，僅憑貸款增長疲弱，較難認定貨幣支持不足。

香港正設法在離岸市場支持這類資本市場發展。據知情人士透露，港交所考慮年底前推出首個債券指數，涵蓋在該交易所上市、使用其基礎設施，且發行額至少人民幣10億元的點心債。行政長官李家超週三表示，指數將提供市場參考，也可作為ETF追蹤標的。今年離岸人民幣主權與公司債發行已達人民幣8,760億元，年增34%，創同期紀錄。

美國外部融資數據則轉弱。7月TIC長期資金淨流出$279億，市場原預期淨流入$1,463億，前期修正後為淨流入$1,744億。整體淨資本流入仍為正的$837億，但低於前期修正後$1,355億；外國債券投資項目則由修正後淨流入$62億，轉為淨流出$36億。

另外，外國持有美國公債餘額減少$504億至$9.25兆，為10月以來最低，減幅以法國與加拿大為主。日本持有額減少$128億至$1.1兆，日本財務省數據顯示，當局很可能出售了部分外國證券，為7月日圓干預籌措資金。持有餘額與交易流量衡量的是海外融資的不同面向，但兩者都顯示7月支持力不如前月。

日本利率變化與干預風險，也促使市場尋找其他融資貨幣。羅素投資與安聯投資指出，瑞士法郎可作為日圓融資的補充；摩根大通的Meera Chandan則看重瑞典克朗與加拿大元，理由是殖利率低，且對全球利率敏感。以日圓融資持有澳元的部位，上半年報酬為9%，7月以來卻虧損1.3%；以瑞郎融資的澳元套利部位，2026年報酬則達14%。

替代貨幣各有弱點。日圓流動性比多數同類貨幣深厚，瑞郎則可能在地緣政治或歐洲政治緊張時急升。安聯的Greg Hirt特別點出明年法國與義大利選舉的風險。融資利率較低的好處，因而可能被負債貨幣升值抵銷。

土耳其出現的是更直接的流動性事件。Pusula Portfoy表示，部分投資基金與貨幣市場基金無法滿足贖回要求後，伊斯坦堡證交所100指數一度下跌6%，觸發全市場熔斷，該基金週三遭遇大量資金流出。這次跌勢有其本地催化因素，即難以應付現金需求，並非單純隨全球利率變動。

## 後續市場觀察

接下來的美國數據將檢驗，零售反彈是否擴及其他經濟領域。9月17日將公布初領失業救濟金人數，共識預估20.8萬人，前值20.6萬人；費城聯準銀行製造業調查預估30.5，前值47.4。其中訂單、就業與價格分項，尤其適合與較弱的紐約服務業讀值對照。市場如今預期的緊縮程度高於官員中位數，因此，活動持續廣泛增強或轉為更明顯放慢的證據，都將影響10月決策。

9月17日的新屋開工與建築許可，將提供實際活動數據，與惡化的建商調查相互比對。新屋開工預估131萬戶，前值123.9萬戶；建築許可預估141萬戶，前值143.3萬戶；成屋待完成銷售預期在下跌2.3%後反彈2%。同日的10年期TIPS標售，將檢驗週三實質殖利率上升、通膨補償下降後，市場承接實質利率風險的意願。週五工業生產預期月增0.3%，將把景氣檢驗範圍延伸至消費者以外。

英國央行9月17日決策，須權衡整體與生產者通膨走強，以及核心、服務業指標穩定；售債計畫則涉及另一個供給問題。日本9月18日會議緊接進口成本激增數據，除了預期升息25個基點，也須留意日本央行預估後續成本轉嫁程度。香港商業銀行即將公布的貸款利率，將決定新一輪基本利率升幅有多少會立即傳至房貸借款人。

沙烏地規劃中的輸油管線局部重啟，是近期最具體的能源觀察點。若實際恢復輸送能力，可在新安排的現貨銷售之外增加交付選項；若延誤，即使美國最新成品油庫存增加，壓力仍會延續。主權信用方面，羅馬尼亞政府組成與2027年預算，將決定發債減少是否同時伴隨更可靠的財政承諾。巴西10月4日大選及很可能舉行的第二輪投票，則使匯率與通膨預期成為本次降息後還能寬鬆多少的關鍵。

overall_summary.headline: 聯準會示意繼續緊縮，美債殖利率曲線趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
聯準會一致決議升息25個基點，將目標區間調至3.75%至4%，為2023年7月以來首次升息。Kevin Warsh將此舉形容為撤除寬鬆，並表示基礎通膨尚未實質改善。2年期美債殖利率上升7個基點至4.74%，10年期微升1個基點至5.01%，30年期則小降1個基點至5.35%。利率交換市場反映明年年中前還將升息三次，路徑比聯準會預測更積極。

8月零售銷售增加1.2%，進口物價上升0.7%，從支出與通膨兩方面強化緊縮理由，但房市與區域服務業已轉弱。油價下跌有助降低長期通膨補償，實質殖利率卻上升，因此長天期名目殖利率變動有限，不等於借款成本普遍減輕。

信用市場維持韌性，美國投資等級債與硬通貨新興市場債利差明顯收窄，高收益債利差則小幅收窄。10家銀行正為Blackstone與Alphabet支持的Crux AI提供$220億晶片擔保貸款。融資意願持續擴大的同時，傳統長天期公司債供給卻因發行人不願鎖定高借款成本而縮減。下一批美國景氣數據將檢驗，需求是否足夠廣泛，能支撐市場目前反映的緊縮路徑。
overall_summary.summary: Warsh對通膨的強硬表態推高市場預期的近期資金成本，但長天期公債守穩、信用利差收窄，顯示投資人仍願意向借款人提供融資。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Short-dated Treasuries fell and the yield curve flattened on Wednesday as the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since July 2023 and signaled that more tightening was likely. The 2-year yield finished 7 basis points higher at 4.74%, while the 10-year edged up 1 basis point to 5.01% and the 30-year slipped 1 basis point to 5.35%. Kevin Warsh's forceful inflation message increased the expected cost of near-term money without provoking another broad retreat from long bonds.

The decision followed a sharp rebound in U.S. retail spending and firmer import prices, although housing and regional services supplied clear evidence of weakness. Falling oil prices helped the inflation outlook at the margin, and long-term inflation compensation declined even as real yields rose. Credit also held up: U.S. investment-grade and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably, while high-yield spreads tightened modestly. The session's defining distinction was between a more restrictive Fed path and continued willingness to finance borrowers, including another enormous AI-infrastructure loan.

## The Fed Raises Rates and Flattens the Curve

The FOMC unanimously raised its target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4%. Warsh described the action as removing accommodation, a characterization that mattered more to the subsequent market adjustment than the widely anticipated increase itself. If the starting point was still supportive of growth, the first increase need not mark the end of the work required to contain inflation.

Warsh said too many goods and services were recording annualized price increases above 3% over six- and 12-month periods. The summer's readings had not persuaded him that the underlying trend was improving materially. At the same time, he described an economy that appeared to be strengthening. The committee emphasized resilient domestic spending, robust capital investment and strong productivity growth, with job gains keeping pace with the workforce and little change in unemployment.

The projections showed a broad coalition for further action. Sixteen of the 18 officials submitting near-term rate forecasts expected at least one more increase by the end of 2026; four projected two additional increases. The median year-end projection rose to 4.1% from 3.8% in June and remained at 4.1% for 2027. Eight officials put the rate at 4.4% next year. Warsh again declined to submit a dot, leaving his own preferred destination outside that distribution.

Officials also raised their median forecast for year-end core inflation to 3.4% from 3.3%, alongside a small increase in projected 2026 GDP growth to 2.3% from 2.2%. Despite tightening, they pushed the expected return to 2% inflation back a year, to 2029. The combination pointed to greater persistence, rather than an increase undertaken because the committee expected an imminent collapse in activity.

Treasuries had rallied before the announcement. The 2-year yield stood near 4.60% immediately before the decision and subsequently climbed to 4.74%, reversing that early improvement. The 10-year also surrendered its earlier decline during Warsh's press conference. By the 5 p.m. New York close, the 5-year was up 3 basis points at 4.86%, between the larger front-end increase and the small move in the benchmark.

The 2s10s spread narrowed 6 basis points to 27 basis points, and 2s30s compressed 8 basis points to 61. That latter gap reached its tightest closing level since March 2025. Over the past month, the 2-year yield has risen 57 basis points against only 10 for the 30-year, leaving the curve substantially flatter as the expected policy path has moved higher.

Inflation-linked securities showed why the limited nominal move at 10 years was not broad borrowing-cost relief. The real yield rose 6 basis points to 2.68%, while the breakeven fell 5 basis points to 2.33%. Investors demanded a higher inflation-adjusted return while accepting less long-term inflation compensation. Lower oil and a more assertive central bank both supported the latter direction; the real-yield increase still tightened the financial hurdle for investment and other long-lived expenditure.

After the decision, swaps incorporated three additional increases by the middle of next year, one more than before the announcement. Money markets assigned roughly a 50% probability to an October increase. That path was more aggressive than the Fed's projections. Capital Economics' Stephen Brown expected the next move in December and another in 2027, arguing that officials were underestimating the possibility of further declines in unemployment.

JPMorgan Asset Management's Priya Misra characterized the shift as one from doubts about Fed credibility toward concern about the economic effects of its inflation campaign. RBC Global Asset Management's Andrzej Skiba thought clear communication could eventually support longer Treasuries after the initial repricing. Evercore's Krishna Guha found the press conference consistently hawkish but warned that describing the move as a removal of accommodation made the eventual destination less clear.

Warsh offered a different diagnosis of the preceding rise in long yields from a simple loss of confidence in the central bank. He cited stronger activity, surging capital spending and competition for funding, explicitly including hyperscalers, as well as geopolitical hotspots and refined-product prices. He rejected the suggestion that market pricing had forced the committee's hand.

The dollar strengthened with the front-end repricing. The Dollar Index gained 0.62% to 100.267, while the S&P 500 fell 0.45%. Semiconductor shares gained 0.63%, helping the Nasdaq 100 finish slightly higher, up 0.03%. Gold futures slipped 0.16% to $4,325.80 an ounce. Those differentiated returns accompanied a tighter policy outlook rather than uniform liquidation across risk assets.

One large bond investor was moving in the opposite direction to the recent selling. JPMorgan Asset Management's Bob Michele said Wednesday that his team had begun buying long-maturity U.S., Japanese and Australian bonds. His view depended on monetary tightening restoring confidence and on possible Middle East stabilization as the U.S. midterm elections approached. He also regarded Treasury buybacks as a stabilizing influence. The prospective geopolitical improvement remained a condition of his argument, not an accomplished development.

President Donald Trump responded to the increase by demanding rates of 1% or less, without initially criticizing Warsh by name. In later remarks Wednesday, he said he had spoken to the chairman and retained confidence in him, while accusing the board of political hostility. The unanimous policy vote thus stood alongside a renewed presidential demand for a sharply different interest-rate setting.

## Spending Rebounds While Housing Weakens

August retail sales supplied a stronger demand foundation before the Fed met. Sales rose 1.2%, the largest increase since March, against a Reuters consensus of 0.8%. July's decline was revised to 0.5% from 0.6%. More importantly for the composition of spending, core sales excluding automobiles, gasoline, building materials and food services jumped 1.4%, compared with a 0.4% forecast, their strongest gain since September 2024.

The response from growth forecasters was immediate. Goldman Sachs raised its Q3 annualized GDP estimate by 0.5 percentage point to 3.0%; JPMorgan lifted its estimate to 3.5% from 2.75%. The strength outside gasoline and vehicles gave the release significance beyond households merely paying more for fuel. It also complicated the assumption that high energy costs and weak confidence were already producing a broad retreat in expenditure.

Import prices reinforced the inflation side of the policy decision. They rose 0.7% in August against a 0.4% consensus, following a revised 0.3% decline in July. Annual growth accelerated to 7.0% from a revised 6.1%, the fastest since August 2022. Export prices increased 0.6% on the month, above the 0.5% consensus and following a revised 1.4% fall; their annual increase reached 8.6%, against a revised 8.1% previously. The traded-goods figures broadened the day's cost evidence alongside the spending rebound.

Other releases showed important limits to that strength. The New York Fed's September services activity index fell to -8.7 from 0.5, recording deterioration in a regional part of the economy. July business inventories increased 0.8%, compared with a 0.3% consensus and a revised 0.1% prior increase. Retail inventories excluding autos also rose 0.8%, versus expectations of 0.7% and a previous 0.5% decline. Faster stockbuilding can support measured output, but its contribution differs from the final-demand strength captured in the retail-sales release.

Housing was already absorbing higher financing costs. The Mortgage Bankers Association's 30-year contract rate rose 12 basis points to 6.97% in the week ended September 11, its highest since May 2025. Total mortgage applications fell 4.1% after a 2.7% decline. Purchase applications slipped 0.8%, while refinancing fell 8.8% to its lowest level since May 2025.

September's NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index then fell 3 points to 32, below the 34 consensus and matching its lowest level since late 2022. Future-sales expectations dropped to their weakest since early 2023, present sales weakened and buyer traffic remained low. Sentiment fell in the South, the largest building region, as well as the Midwest and Northeast; the West improved slightly.

Builders were making more concessions without escaping cost pressure. The share offering incentives rose to 66% from 63%, while those cutting prices increased to 38% from 35%. NAHB Chairman Bill Owens cited higher materials and fuel costs alongside persistent labor shortages. In some markets, he said, increased immigration enforcement was discouraging even legal workers from attending job sites. Weak demand therefore coexisted with constraints that made construction more expensive.

The broader consumer-facing corporate picture was similarly uneven. More than a quarter of stocks in the S&P 500 Consumer Discretionary Index were at 52-week lows, despite the strong spending release. CIBC Capital Markets estimated that AI investment would contribute roughly 0.4 percentage point to annual inflation this year. That estimate identifies a source of price pressure outside household demand, helping explain why businesses exposed to financing costs and constrained consumers can struggle while aggregate spending remains resilient.

Oil moved favorably during Wednesday's session. Brent fell 3.47% to $104.98 a barrel and WTI lost 4.09% to $101.50 at the fixed-income close. The retreat reduced the immediate energy impulse, although Brent remained 18.59% higher over the month. Saudi Aramco had sold about 20 million barrels to Asian refiners for collection outside Hormuz, a change in delivery arrangements after the East-West pipeline shutdown.

U.S. petroleum inventories also provided some relief from the scarcity picture. EIA crude stocks fell 0.64 million barrels in the week ended September 11, less than the expected 1.6 million-barrel draw. Gasoline inventories rose 0.794 million barrels against an expected decline of 1 million, while distillates increased 1.585 million against a projected 0.1 million build. Product accumulation was a useful counterweight to overseas disruption and high fuel prices.

Later Wednesday reporting gave the Saudi repair effort a more concrete timetable. Aramco was working to bypass a damaged section of the 1,200-kilometer East-West line, seeking to restore about half its capacity within days and full operation in roughly six weeks. That remained a repair plan rather than restored throughput, but it narrowed the immediate question from an indefinite closure to the execution of a partial restart.

## AI Financing Expands as Long Corporate Supply Shrinks

Ten banks are providing a $22 billion loan for Crux AI, the cloud venture backed by Blackstone and Alphabet, according to people familiar with the financing. The money will buy Google's tensor processing units, with the chips' value and customer contracts backing the debt. The transaction moves a large new funding commitment into the processors that fill data centers, rather than construction alone.

Goldman Sachs, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking, Barclays, BNP Paribas and Bank of Nova Scotia are among the participating banks. The group is bringing in additional lenders through syndication to share the exposure. Some banks are also providing a $1 billion revolving facility, while the main loan could eventually be replaced by longer-term institutional financing in the investment-grade bond market.

Crux aims to bring 500 megawatts online in 2027 and has initial equity backing of $5 billion from Blackstone. Its planned customers include AI laboratories, putting it in competition with cloud-capacity providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius. Delays at major intended data-center sites remain a practical complication: the financing supports chips and customer commitments whose deployment still depends on facilities becoming available.

The scale of related prospective transactions is growing as well. Another chip-financing structure of more than $60 billion is under discussion, following a $35 billion package backed by Broadcom to support Anthropic's TPU leasing. Separately, OpenAI is holding early talks about a funding round valuing it at more than $1.2 trillion. That potential equity raise could provide more scope for acquisitions and for postponing a public listing; it is not yet completed capital.

Europe is preparing to take a larger role in the debt funding. Goldman Sachs estimates that $5 billion-$10 billion of data-center bonds could reach European markets by year-end, followed by a larger wave in 2027. JPMorgan and Goldman have assembled specialist teams to pursue that business. European AI-related debt accounts for about 5% of high-yield issuance, compared with 19% in the United States, according to Dealogic and Goldman research.

The projects are becoming too large for the financing mix used in earlier developments. Portugal's planned 1.2-gigawatt Start Campus is one example. Goldman's Miriam Wheeler said a new European center of 100-200 megawatts could require debt deals of at least $1 billion-$2 billion, with larger projects drawing on investment-grade, high-yield and 144A markets. She estimated that Europe's share of the global AI buildout could rise to as much as 25% from 10%. Bloomberg Intelligence puts potential European requirements for cloud infrastructure, data centers and other critical technologies at about $3 trillion through 2035.

Credit investors are nevertheless distinguishing between projects. CoreWeave's bonds, the sole data-center issues in Europe's high-yield market, have traded below par since news that major customer Meta was developing a competing cloud-infrastructure business. RBC BlueBay's Sid Chhabra emphasized a high diligence threshold, while lenders with environmental mandates are scrutinizing power and water use. The potential issuance expansion brings customer concentration and unfinished construction directly into underwriting decisions.

A smaller completed financing illustrates the interest available for acceptable structures. Equinix's GBP280 million asset-backed offering in July attracted more than GBP510 million of orders after some European investors visited its Slough facilities. Those buyers were examining physical assets and operations before a much larger prospective supply wave, rather than treating every AI-related borrower as interchangeable.

In a separate later-Wednesday announcement, EQT's chairman said the firm plans to invest $50 billion in India by 2030. Around $30 billion would go to data centers and another $5 billion to renewable power, including a significant investment in Gautam Adani's data-center business. Those are prospective commitments, but their combination of computing capacity and electricity shows the breadth of capital required beyond chips.

Meanwhile, conventional long-dated corporate issuance is contracting as issuers resist locking in high borrowing costs. Long-maturity notes represented just 5% of September U.S. high-grade sales, the smallest share since at least 2020, and their volume was less than half the year-earlier amount. The share maturing in three to 10 years increased to 60% from 51%. Companies and banks have been abandoning planned long offerings, according to people familiar with the market.

That scarcity is supporting demand when such debt does appear. Newly reported detail on Aon's Monday financing showed more than $14 billion of orders for its $2 billion 2056 tranche, which subsequently outperformed the other maturities in the secondary market. GSK's $500 million 30-year tranche last week attracted orders equal to 15 times the offering. Insurers and pension funds still need long assets even as corporate treasurers become less willing to supply them.

The interaction with government borrowing is increasingly material. Bloomberg's newly reported calculation found that Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle had collectively added about $412 billion to debt obligations over five years. Warsh's reference to competition for capital therefore concerns a substantial expansion by highly rated borrowers, not only speculative projects.

Fresh Wells Fargo research examined the fiscal side of the growth argument. In a Tuesday note, economists Tom Porcelli and Michael Pugliese calculated that stabilizing U.S. debt relative to GDP over the next decade would require annual growth of 3%-3.5% and no major changes to tax or spending policy. With slower labor-force expansion, they said achieving that growth would require the fastest labor-productivity performance on record. The estimate sets demanding conditions for growth to offset the debt burden even as current investment supports activity.

Xerox faces a more immediate balance-sheet choice. Starteepo's Frantisek Bostl, whose fund holds an approximately 7.3% economic interest, is pressing for advisers to examine a joint venture, capital partnership or sale of the financial-services operation. He argues that proceeds could reduce debt and simplify the company. Xerox has said it will review the proposals; Bostl said he would explore other options if they were not implemented by Q3. This remains shareholder pressure for an asset transaction, not an agreed disposal.

## Inflation Signals Diverge Across Central Banks

Britain's August CPI rose to 3.1%, a five-month high and in line with the Reuters consensus, but the underlying measures were steadier. Core inflation held at 2.6% for a fourth month and services inflation remained at 3.4%. Producer prices were less reassuring: output prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, exceeding every forecast after July was revised to 3.3%. Input inflation reached 6.1%, with July revised to 5.8% from 4.9%.

The divide matters for the Bank of England because higher energy and transport prices have yet to produce an equivalent acceleration in those broad underlying consumer measures. Wednesday market pricing assigned roughly a 20% chance to a 25-basis-point increase on September 17 and about a 75% chance of two increases by year-end. The immediate decision and the prospect of later tightening remained distinct judgments.

New analysis of Britain's debt structure also showed why reduced long-bond supply has not delivered durable relief. The weighted average maturity of government debt has fallen to about 11 years from more than 18 in 2020 as issuance shifts toward shorter maturities and pension demand weakens. Bloomberg Economics estimated that higher borrowing costs and inflation could consume about GBP16 billion of the government's GBP23.6 billion fiscal-rule buffer.

RBC strategist Megum Muhic judged that even halting the BoE's long-gilt sales would have only a marginal effect amid wider global pressures. Yet the spread of 30-year gilts over comparable swaps has been broadly steady this year, tempering the argument that the entire yield increase represents a sharply worsening UK-specific fiscal premium. The reduced maturity of the debt stock and the diminished fiscal buffer are separate vulnerabilities even when that relative-risk measure is stable.

Euro-area wage evidence offered a counterweight to energy inflation. Annual labor-cost growth slowed to 3.1% in Q2 from 3.3% in Q1. The ECB's wage tracker projected 2.7% growth in Q1 2027 and 2.8% in Q2, a modest pickup rather than a return to 2024's 5.2% peak. The bank said the depressed first-half 2026 readings partly reflected the disappearance of earlier one-off payments, an effect that fully dissipates in the second half.

The fresh figures support a distinction between mechanically firmer wage comparisons and a broad response to the energy shock. The ECB regards wage growth near 3% as broadly consistent with 2% inflation. Its warning remains that a prolonged shock could alter wage and price behavior, but the current tracker gives little evidence of that acceleration already occurring.

European sovereign bonds recovered some ground before the Fed decision. In late-morning European trading, Germany's 10-year yield was down 3 basis points at 3.504%, after Tuesday's 3.5723% peak, the highest since June 2009. France's yield fell 3 basis points to 4.468%, leaving its spread over Germany at 96 basis points, while Italy's yield declined 4 basis points to 4.38%. Lower oil brought duration relief without eliminating the large French risk premium or expectations of further ECB tightening.

Bank of Canada's newly published September 2 deliberations defined its inflation condition more explicitly. Policymakers had held at 2.25% and saw little evidence that gasoline prices were passing broadly into other goods and services. They nevertheless agreed that persistent energy costs made spillovers more likely and that broader CPI effects could require a monetary response. Headline inflation had hovered near 3%, whereas core inflation was near the 2% target.

Council members differed over the amount of slack but still judged the economy to be in excess supply, despite broadening growth and solid job gains. New U.S. tariffs covering about 5% of Canadian goods exports to the United States would hurt affected businesses and confidence, they said, although the direct aggregate effect would likely be modest and fiscal measures could offset some damage. Canada's counter-tariffs were expected to have a muted inflation effect because they concentrated on intermediate inputs and products with domestic substitutes.

An independent trade-policy development came from Ursula von der Leyen, who invited Canada to become the EU's first associate member. The proposed status has no existing treaty definition. Its significance for investment and trade will depend on the terms rather than the title, with Mark Carney due to address the European Parliament on Thursday.

Japan's August trade figures showed an increasingly expensive energy bill before its own policy decision. Imports rose 28.0% from a year earlier, the fastest since November 2022 and above the 26.3% forecast. Exports increased 19.3%, exceeding the 18.2% consensus and extending their run of annual gains to 12 months. The trade deficit reached JPY1.106 trillion against a JPY1.053 trillion forecast.

Crude import volumes rose just 3.6%, compared with a 58.7% increase in value. That difference identifies prices as the dominant pressure on the oil bill. Analysts cited by Reuters warned that import lags could make the pass-through worse from September, adding a fresh observation to expectations of BOJ tightening.

South Africa's expectations survey moved favorably instead. The Bureau for Economic Research reported that average inflation expectations two years ahead fell to 3.8% from 3.9%, still above the central bank's 3% goal. Forward-rate agreements reduced the implied probability of a September 23 quarter-point increase to 52% from 56% Tuesday. Amundi's Nicolas Dahan warned that another hold could damage credibility, while Governor Lesetja Kganyago has advocated a measured response to overlapping oil and weather shocks.

After the U.S. close, Brazil delivered its fifth consecutive 25-basis-point cut, unanimously lowering Selic to 13.75%. Cumulative easing since March reached 125 basis points. The central bank kept its relevant-horizon inflation forecast at 3.2% for Q1 2028 and left the ultimate size of the cycle dependent on information needed to secure convergence to target.

Earlier Wednesday, Brazil's economic-activity index had fallen 0.22% in July, a second consecutive monthly decline and slightly weaker than the expected 0.2% drop; activity was still 1.14% higher than a year earlier. That fresh weakening supports the cut, but the October election creates exchange-rate uncertainty. Goldman Sachs' Alberto Ramos said a sharp real selloff could cause a pause. XP's Caio Megale expected two further quarter-point cuts this year, whereas Itau's Diogo Guillen favored a stop at 13.75%, allowing that stable exchange rates and inflation forecasts could permit more easing.

Early Thursday in Asia, the IMF urged Australia's central bank to remain ready to raise rates if necessary. Its Article IV mission cut growth forecasts to 1.9% for 2026 and 1.6% for 2027, from 2% and 1.7%, but still saw upside inflation risks and uncertainty about whether financial conditions were restrictive enough. It also identified data-center investment as a source of construction pressure and potentially higher electricity costs, while arguing that fiscal restraint would help disinflation.

Hong Kong then followed the Fed with a 25-basis-point increase in its benchmark to 4.25%. The early-Thursday move protects the currency peg, but mortgage pricing also depends on commercial-bank lending rates and local liquidity. One-month Hibor had reached 2.95%, its highest in almost three months, while the Hong Kong dollar traded near the weak end of its permitted band. Higher U.S. returns continue to encourage demand for dollars even as local borrowing costs threaten the property recovery.

## Sovereign Funding and Local Markets Find Different Buyers

Romania's foreign-currency bonds rallied after officials told investors that this year's international issuance would probably be reduced. Treasury chief Stefan Nanu said no further eurobonds would be sold until a government was formed and the political outlook became clearer, according to people familiar with a London meeting. Bonds maturing in 2051 and 2053 were among emerging markets' strongest performers after the report.

Romania has raised about EUR5 billion in international euro- and dollar-denominated tranches against an original EUR10 billion external target, and official figures separately show roughly EUR2 billion of private placements. Increased domestic borrowing has reduced the immediate need for additional international sales. The supply news supported prices without resolving the challenge of agreeing a credible 2027 budget.

Current relative valuations show the compensation investors are receiving for that risk. Five-year Romanian CDS stood at 144 basis points Tuesday, down from 167 at end-April but far above roughly 85 for Oman and Indonesia. Romania retains the lowest investment-grade rating at the major agencies, yet its foreign debt trades at levels comparable with several speculative-grade sovereigns. Its 2-year local yield of 6.52% was about 180 basis points above Poland and 235 above the Czech Republic.

Aberdeen's Viktor Szabo saw value if policy rates remained stable and fiscal performance stayed strong, but warned that an unconvincing 2027 budget could precipitate a downgrade. Societe Generale's Juan Orts expected Romania to avoid a cut at S&P's review next month. The immediate rally followed reduced prospective supply; those differing fiscal judgments determine how durable the improvement may be.

Senegal received a new route into benchmark-tracked local debt. JPMorgan's forthcoming Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets Edge will include two Senegalese instruments valued at $654 million, giving the country a 0.34% weight. Africa will represent almost 45% of the index, with Egypt and Morocco each at 8%. Across all regions, it will track about $328 billion in 425 instruments spanning 26 markets and 24 currencies.

The inclusion concerns local obligations, which Senegal intends to exclude from its external debt treatment. Its sovereign risk premium over Treasuries remains 1,639 basis points in a separate JPMorgan measure. Benchmark eligibility therefore introduces a different potential investor base without changing the status of negotiations over external claims.

In India, fresh forecasts extended the implications of the RBI's already announced liquidity withdrawal. ICICI Securities Primary Dealership and IDFC First Bank see the 10-year yield potentially reaching 7.25% by year-end, above the 7.08% level described after Tuesday's selloff. Citi brought its expected first rate increase forward to October from December. QuantEco estimated that another INR2 trillion of liquidity would need to be absorbed, potentially through short-term FX swaps, stabilization securities or cash-management bills.

BNP Paribas strategist Chandresh Jain expected continuing pressure in three- to 10-year debt as banks reduced positions accumulated with surplus cash, with three- to five-year yields potentially rising faster than the 10-year. Newly reported foreign holdings data showed an INR24.7 billion reduction in index-eligible bonds Tuesday after an INR47.3 billion outflow Friday. Those figures add an investor-flow dimension to the adjustment already underway in local rates.

China's central-bank governor offered a structural interpretation of weak lending rather than a new stimulus promise. Pan Gongsheng said shrinking property and local-government financing demand was outweighing borrowing by emerging industries. Outstanding loans exceed CNY280 trillion, but high-tech manufacturing and green technology, which contributed more than 40% of first-half growth, depend less on bank credit.

Pan highlighted a change in financing composition: in 2025, loans represented 45% of the increase in total social financing, while bonds and equities together accounted for 47%, surpassing loans for the first time. He described financing conditions as relatively accommodative and slower aggregate expansion as helpful for stabilizing leverage. His argument reduces the force of weak loan growth alone as a signal of insufficient monetary support.

Hong Kong is seeking to support that capital-market development offshore. HKEX is considering launching its first bond index before year-end, covering dim sum issues of at least CNY1 billion that are listed on the exchange and use its infrastructure, according to people familiar with the plans. Chief Executive John Lee said Wednesday that it would provide a market reference and a basis for ETFs. Offshore yuan sovereign and corporate issuance has reached CNY876 billion this year, up 34% and a record for the period.

U.S. external-financing figures moved the other way. July net long-term TIC flows showed a $27.9 billion outflow against an expected $146.3 billion inflow and a revised $174.4 billion prior inflow. Overall net capital inflows remained positive at $83.7 billion, down from a revised $135.5 billion. The foreign-bond investment series recorded a $3.6 billion outflow after a revised $6.2 billion inflow.

Separately, foreign Treasury holdings fell $50.4 billion to $9.25 trillion, their lowest since October, led by France and Canada. Japan's holdings declined $12.8 billion to $1.1 trillion. Japan's Finance Ministry figures indicated that authorities likely sold some foreign securities to finance July yen intervention. The holdings decline and the transaction-flow measures describe different aspects of overseas financing, while both give a less supportive July picture than the preceding month.

The search for alternative funding currencies is another consequence of Japan's changing rates and intervention risk. Russell Investments and Allianz Global Investors identified the Swiss franc as a possible complement to yen funding; JPMorgan's Meera Chandan highlighted the krona and Canadian dollar because of low yields and sensitivity to global rates. A yen-funded Australian-dollar position lost 1.3% since July after returning 9% in the first half, whereas franc-funded carry into the Australian dollar had returned 14% in 2026.

The alternatives carry different vulnerabilities. The yen has deeper liquidity than most peers, while the franc can appreciate sharply during geopolitical or European political stress. Allianz's Greg Hirt specifically highlighted the risk surrounding next year's French and Italian elections. A lower funding rate can therefore be offset by a rising liability currency.

Turkey supplied a more immediate liquidity event. The Borsa Istanbul 100 fell as much as 6%, triggering a market-wide circuit breaker, after Pusula Portfoy said some investment and money-market funds could not meet redemption requests. The fund experienced large outflows Wednesday. The difficulty meeting cash demands, rather than a general change in global rates alone, gave the Turkish selloff its own local catalyst.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. releases will test how broadly the retail rebound extends. September 17 brings initial unemployment claims, with consensus at 208,000 after 206,000, and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey, expected at 30.5 after 47.4. Its orders, employment and price components will be particularly useful alongside the weaker New York services reading. The market now anticipates more tightening than the median policymaker, making evidence of either sustained breadth or a sharper slowdown consequential for the October decision.

Housing starts and permits on September 17 will put hard activity beside the deteriorating builder survey. Starts are expected at 1.31 million after 1.239 million and permits at 1.41 million after 1.433 million; pending-home sales are expected to rebound 2% after a 2.3% fall. The 10-year TIPS auction that day tests demand for real duration after Wednesday's rise in real yields and fall in inflation compensation. Friday's industrial-production release, with a 0.3% monthly increase expected, extends the activity test beyond consumers.

The Bank of England's September 17 decision must reconcile firmer headline and producer inflation with stable core and services measures, while its bond-sale plans address a separate supply question. Japan's September 18 meeting follows the import-cost surge; the extent to which the BOJ anticipates further pass-through matters alongside the expected quarter-point increase. In Hong Kong, commercial banks' forthcoming lending-rate announcements will determine how much of the new benchmark increase reaches mortgage borrowers immediately.

Saudi Arabia's planned partial pipeline restart is the most concrete near-term energy test. Actual restored capacity would improve delivery options beyond the newly arranged spot sales, while delays would prolong the pressure despite the latest U.S. product-stock builds. In sovereign credit, Romania's government formation and 2027 budget will determine whether reduced issuance is accompanied by stronger fiscal assurance. Brazil's October 4 election and likely runoff leave the exchange rate and inflation expectations central to how much additional easing can follow the latest cut.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
The Fed unanimously raised its target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4%, its first increase since July 2023. Kevin Warsh described the move as removing accommodation and said underlying inflation had not improved materially. The 2-year Treasury yield rose 7 basis points to 4.74%, while the 10-year edged up 1 basis point to 5.01% and the 30-year slipped 1 basis point to 5.35%. Swaps priced three further increases by the middle of next year, a more aggressive path than the Fed's projections.

August retail sales rose 1.2% and import prices increased 0.7%, reinforcing the spending and inflation case for tightening, even as housing and regional services weakened. Falling oil helped reduce long-term inflation compensation, but higher real yields meant the limited move in nominal long yields was not broad borrowing-cost relief.

Credit remained resilient: U.S. investment-grade and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably, while high-yield spreads tightened modestly. Ten banks are providing a $22 billion chip-backed loan for Blackstone- and Alphabet-backed Crux AI. That expanding financing appetite coexists with shrinking conventional long-dated corporate supply as issuers resist locking in high borrowing costs. The next U.S. activity releases will test whether demand is broad enough to sustain the tightening path now priced by markets.
